document.title: Roger Pardo-Maurer email, "Greetings from scenic Kandahar," with Rumsfeld snowflake cover note to Larry Di Rita, "E-mail"
document.authors: Combined Joint Special Operations Task Force, Coalition Coordination Cell, Kandahar (Roger Pardo-Maurer); cover note by Donald Rumsfeld (Sept 13, 2002)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Afghanistan 20/20: The 20-Year War in 20 Documents | National Security Archive
document.note: [Unclassified] Candid, humorous 14-page email by a Green Beret hunting high-value targets in Kandahar. It warns that border provinces still swarm with 'Bad Guys' (Pakistan as a Taliban sanctuary), recommends a Special Forces approach of fighting alongside Afghans, and says Afghanistan is not really a country. Rumsfeld requested a copy in a Sept 13, 2002 snowflake.

events.description: Rumsfeld sends snowflake to Larry Di Rita asking to read the Pardo-Maurer email.
Pardo-Maurer completes email from Kandahar dated Aug 11-15, 2002 describing SF life and coalition forces.
Pardo-Maurer activated to join B Company, 3rd Battalion, 20th Special Forces.
Mullah Omar wraps himself in the Cloak of the Prophet at Kandahar and proclaims the Age of Taliban (historical reference).
US attack on Deh Rawod, allegedly hitting a wedding party; the Kandahar governor organized five neighboring governors to demand clearance of US operations; operations reportedly froze for a month.
Pardo-Maurer and Weatherford attend a lunch and payout hosted by Major General Razik Shirzai at his fort near Kandahar.
A bomb was left in the Kandahar flight terminal about 100 yards from the author.
Hakim Tanewal declared that 'the time for warlords is over'; Pacha Khan replied to the Christian Science Monitor with a threat.
Pardo-Maurer activated for service and joined B Company, 3rd Battalion, 20th Special Forces.
Pardo-Maurer's e-mail written from Kandahar, dated August 11-15, 2002.
Rumsfeld snowflake to Di Rita asking to read the e-mail.
Mullah Omar wrapped himself in the Cloak of the Prophet at Kandahar fort and proclaimed the Age of Taliban.
Battle of Navas de Tolosa in which Aznar Pardo allegedly burned the Almohad palenque.
Flash flood washed away a convoy of unit Humvees at Jalalabad.
Aznar Pardo burned the palenque of the Almohad at the battle of Navas de Tolosa.
Mullah Omar wrapped himself in the Cloak of the Prophet and proclaimed the Age of Taliban from the fort walls.
Soviet engineers' bones unearthed at Bagram while digging a drain.
SEALs banished from the Kiwi courtyard by Steve after vandalism.
Tanewal issued a manifesto declaring the time for warlords is over; Pacha Khan responded in an interview with the Christian Science Monitor that calling them warlords would get you killed.
Pardo-Maurer and Weatherford dined with Major General Razik Shiriai and about 500 guests at his fort.
Two hand grenades were thrown over a wall at the author's Master Sergeant; another US soldier was shot through both cheeks in Kandahar bazaar.
US strike on Deh Rawod, which may have hit a wedding party, called in by an SF team after locals fired on US planes.
The Governor of Kandahar organised five neighboring governors to demand that US operations be cleared through them; the US refused and Karzai posed as honest broker.
A bomb was left in the flight terminal at Kandahar airfield about 100 yards from the author.
Two hand grenades were thrown over a wall at the author's Master Sergeant last weekend; a US soldier was shot in the face in Kandahar bazaar.
Norwegian and Danish contingents left Kandahar, cutting the alcohol supply pipeline for allies.
actors: Combined Joint Special Operations Task Force

events.description: German resupply plane breakdown left SF Village temporarily dry.
Young SEALs banished from the NZ SAS courtyard by commander Steve after misbehavior.
82nd Airborne officers complain weekly about SF dress and grooming; 82nd taking most casualties from Taliban/al-Qaida ambushes.
Pardo-Maurer and Weatherford attend a lunch with General Razik Shirzai and about 500 followers at his fort, where he distributes money and contraband.
Hakim Tanewal declares 'the time for warlords is over'; Pacha Khan responds in an interview that he'll kill those who call them warlords.
Karzai appoints Hakim Tanewal as governor, the fifth appointee in five months, but the post is on hold pending Pacha Khan disbanding militias.

sources_cited: Christian Science Monitor interview with Pacha Khan
key_claims: As of August 2002, US Special Forces and coalition partners (Germany, Canada, New Zealand) were based at Kandahar Air Field, the former Taliban stronghold.
The Taliban and al-Qa'ida had reverted from formations to small-scale ambush and harassment, making heavy 82nd Airborne maneuver forces poorly suited.
B Company's area of operations spanned Kandahar, Zabul, Oruzgan, Ghazni and Paktika up to the Pakistani border.
Mullah Omar's Cloak of the Prophet episode in Kandahar is cited as the Taliban's symbolic origin, and he carried a $10 million FBI reward.

The author argues the Deh Rawod strike was exploited by Afghan warlords to gain leverage over Karzai and the US, and operations froze for a month while Al Qaeda and Taliban reconsolidated out of Pakistan.
Al Qaeda is said to be regrouping in southeastern Afghanistan with the connivance of junior warlords and double-dealing Pakistanis.
The core political dynamic is the power struggle between Karzai and Defense Minister Fahim Khan, who personally commands more and better troops than his ministry.
Pacha Khan controls Paktia and blocks Karzai's appointee Hakim Tanewal from taking the governorship.
Razik Shirzai, brother of the Kandahar governor, holds a US contract to secure Kandahar Airfield and allegedly extorts smugglers at Spin Boldak.
The author claims US forces are detaining Taliban and Saudi, Yemeni, Chechen and Pakistani al-Qaeda members, and warns against a conventional approach or nation-building.
